portion_doctrine: Segments 71-80 contain a transcript-heavy corpus of Photoshop and Adobe Firefly tutorials spanning foundational UI navigation, advanced color grading, photo manipulation techniques, retouching workflows (manual vs AI comparison), and modern generative AI integration. Content oscillates between educational video scripts from PIXimperfect tutorials and technical Firefly/Photoshop masterclass streams. Central theme: operationalizing both legacy precision-based editing and emerging generative fill capabilities within a unified Adobe stack. NO em-dashes detected in source. Bulk boilerplate ads/sponsor mentions/CTA/navigation UI present but non-core.
operating_rules: Color grading requires reference sampling from source images (eyedropper + curves RGB channel manipulation) for tonal accuracy across shadows/midtones/highlights
Mask-first workflow: all adjustment layers should include inverted masks (Ctrl+I) before painting to preserve non-target areas
Hue saturation targeting via hand tool (click-drag on subject color) + slider range expansion yields more natural color shifts than global saturation changes
Dodge/burn foundation: soft light blend mode at 1-2% flow prevents over-flattening; requires contrast check layer baseline before application
Photoshop generative fill intelligently analyzes scene composition (perspective, light direction, depth cues) vs content-aware fill which only samples adjacent pixels
Generative expand on video requires stationary camera (no motion tracking support currently)
Selection-first gate: always expand selections 20px before generative fill to give algorithm boundary context
Oil painting effect via channels: fill new channel at 40% brightness, select from channel, then generative fill with painting style prompt
Frequency separation workflow: median blur layer + high-pass layer (1.8px) + linear light blend = non-destructive skin texture
Scale factor rule: generative fill resolution ~1200x1200; massive selections on large images yield low-res output (use smaller chunks instead)
Blend mode hierarchy for retouching: soft light for subtle sculpting, multiply for shadows, screen for highlights, linear light for texture

gates: Selection-before-generative-fill: always expand selection 20px before running generative fill to provide boundary context to algorithm
Mask-inversion mandate: every adjustment layer receiving brush work must be inverted (Ctrl+I) first to prevent off-target edits
Reference sampling gate: color grading requires eyedropper sampling from source image before curve adjustments (no guessing)
Flow calibration (dodge/burn): soft light blend mode layers must be set to 1-2% flow to prevent flattening contrast
High-pass radius parity: high-pass filter radius MUST match Gaussian blur radius on color layer (typically 1.8px for frequency separation)
Video stationarity check: generative expand on video only works with stationary camera (no motion tracking support currently)
Channel brightness threshold: oil painting effect requires 40% brightness fill in new channel (too low misses selection, too high over-selects)
Resolution awareness: generative fill performance drops on selections >1200x1200 pixels (split large selections into chunks)
contradictions: PHOTOSHOP CURVES vs CAMERA RAW: Photoshop curves + hue saturation cannot match Camera Raw's refined saturation slider (50% midpoint control unavailable natively in Photoshop; workaround requires layer blend mode + opacity manipulation)

CONTENT AWARE vs GENERATIVE: Content-aware fill is presented as legacy/inferior (only samples adjacent pixels) but generative fill is context-aware scene analysis. Yet tutorials show content-aware in some situations works adequately (contradiction in 'always use generative' framing)

MANUAL vs AI RETOUCHING: Tutorial series runs 'AI vs human' comparison suggesting human dodge/burn yields better quality than retouch-for-me plugin automation, yet then advocates hybrid approach (AI heavy lifting + human fine-tuning). Unclear which is the recommended primary workflow
BLEND MODE OPACITY: Dodge/burn soft light layer recommended at both 100% (for full effect comparison) AND 60-72% (for 'natural look'). Contradictory guidance on when to use which threshold
SELECTION EXPANSION TIMING: One method expands selection BEFORE generative fill. Another method includes selection boundaries as part of prompt. Inconsistent sequencing between tutorials
weird_gold: CHANNEL-BASED OIL PAINTING HACK: Filling a new channel at exactly 40% brightness, then selecting from that channel (CTL+click), then running generative fill with 'oil painting' prompt will preserve 40% of original image pixels while generating painting effect on remaining 60%. This is non-obvious and not discoverable from UI alone (learned from blue Lightning TV via video learner)

BLEND IF ALT-CLICK TRANSITION SOFTENING: Holding ALT while clicking the blend-if slider splits it into two values, creating smooth transition between blend ranges. This is buried in layer style dialog and rarely mentioned in beginner tutorials

REFINED SATURATION SLIDER EXISTS IN CAMERA RAW BUT NOT PHOTOSHOP: Camera Raw filter has a 50% midpoint 'refined saturation' slider that prevents color bleeding during curves adjustments. Native Photoshop curves has no equivalent (workaround: Camera Raw as smart filter or layer blend modes)

GENERATIVE FILL RECOGNIZES IMPLICIT TOOL SUBSTITUTION: Replacing 'fork with spoon' in ice cream bowl shows generative fill understands semantic tool-context relationships, not just color/texture replacement

PERSPECTIVE RECONSTRUCTION IN GENERATIVE FILL: Removing people from fountain courtyard image shows generative fill recreates perspective-correct arches/columns at bottom of frame. This suggests 3D spatial reasoning within 2D image
STATIONARY-ONLY VIDEO CONSTRAINT: Generative expand works on video but only if camera doesn't move (no motion tracking). This is a hard gate not present in motion-aware video tools (Runway, etc.)

FIREFLY CREDIT ECONOMY: 500 credits per Luma Ray 3 video = $2.50 at $10/month (2000 credits) plan. A 200-shot short film requires 5 generations per shot = 1000 clips = $2500 cost. This creates inverse relationship between creative ambition and affordability

QUICK SELECTION AUTO-DETECTS CONTEXT: Quick selection tool with 'select subject' + object detection enabled automatically detects bicycles, people, objects without manual refinement in many cases. This represents paradigm shift from manual selection to ML-driven detection
